english.title: Disclose / threaten to disclose private sexual photographs and films with intent to cause distress

english.notes:
(i) This section and the associated offence are repealed from 30th January 2024 due to changes made by the Online Safety Act 2023. For the replacement offences applying from the 31st January 2024, see section 66B of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and the following offence documents: H101570 - Sharing photograph or film of person in intimate state without consent; H101571 - Sharing photograph or film of person in intimate state intending to cause alarm distress or humiliation; H101572 - Sharing photograph or film of person in intimate state for the purpose of sexual gratification; H101573 - Threatening to share photograph or film of person in intimate state.(ii) This offence includes 'to disclose' or 'threats to disclose' with effect from the 29th June 2021. Prior to this date, it was only an offence 'to disclose' - see H12033 for details.
(iii) The offence is not committed if the disclosure of the photograph or film is made to the individual who appears in the photo/film.
(iv) Where a person is charged with an offence under this section of threatening to disclose a private sexual photograph or film, it is not necessary for the prosecution to prove -
(a) that the photograph or film referred to in the threat exists, or
(b) if it does exist, that it is in fact a private sexual photograph or film.
(v) A person charged with an offence under this section is not to be taken to have intended to cause distress by disclosing, or threatening to disclose, a photograph or film merely because that was a natural and probable consequence of the disclosure or threat.
(vi) Various defences are outlined in section 33(3) - (6).
(vii) Schedule 8 to the Act makes special provision in connection with the operation of section 33 in relation to persons providing information society services.
